chunks: But for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is compassionate and kind.

key_terms.رَءُوفٌ: Compassionate; showing deep affection and pity
key_terms.رَحْمَتُهُ: His mercy; divine compassion and mercy
key_terms.فَضْلُ: Grace or bounty; a special favor bestowed by God

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's grace and mercy towards humanity?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate that divine grace (fadl) and mercy (rahmah) are not merely abstract attributes but the active causes of human salvation and spiritual elevation. It underscores the theological principle that God’s inherent compassion (ra'uf) and kindness (rahim) serve as the ultimate justification for His guidance, distinguishing His benevolence from mere obligation.
